svg.title: Where mountain gorillas live
svg.desc: A simplified map of the border region where the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda and Rwanda meet, beside Lake Kivu. Mountain gorillas live in only two forests about 25 km apart: the Virunga volcanoes, which hold 604 gorillas and span all three countries, and Bwindi Impenetrable Forest in Uganda, which holds 459. Together that is about 1,063 animals in roughly 790 square kilometres, and none live in captivity.

text.font-family: Georgia, serif
-apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Two patches of forest, 25 to 50 km apart. That is the whole world for this animal.
